summary: Coverage baseline for the daily ingestion workflow. 'observed' is the coverage confirmed when this baseline was accepted; 'floor' is the alarm threshold, set at or below observed to tolerate normal per-source variance. The run fails when coverage drops below a floor (a regression), reports 'degraded' while documented gaps remain open, and asks for the baseline to be raised when coverage rises above observed.

intelligence.reason: Several governed publishers reject automated retrieval (HTTP 403) or expose no authoritative original-page evidence. The floor sits below observed because per-source availability fluctuates daily.

blog.reason: All four governed blog sources currently fail publication: World Bank and ISS expose no machine-readable publication evidence, and AfDB/UNECA feeds are refused or yield no admissible dated candidates.

commodity.reason: Only cobalt and copper expose a current dated quote with valid unit and currency. Lithium, gold, and bauxite have no free source publishing admissible current quote evidence; Guinea bauxite FOB needs a licensed benchmark. The floor equals observed because losing either remaining identity is material.
